The row stays OPEN.'), and /sliceStanding/noSealedRow and /sliceStanding/keychainStanding were both added. The closure sentence is therefore false as written.
shouldFix.secondInstance: The same roster is inaccurate in the opposite direction. It names /authorityClaim and states explicitly that '/date is on this roster', but the diff shows neither changed: /authorityClaim is byte-identical between v1 and v2, and /date is '2026-08-15' in both. So the roster simultaneously omits a field that moved and claims two that did not. It is not a description of the change set in either direction.
shouldFix.whyThisIsAFinding: The roster exists to bound a re-read: a coordinator who trusts it will re-read the listed paths and skip the rest. Here the skipped field is the one that carries this artifact's D-096 (A) sentence — and 'never mint a D-096 (A) grant' is a standing instruction on every dispatch in this corpus. A roster-bounded re-read would not look at the field whose D-096 (A) wording changed. That is exactly the cost that separates a rostered-path miss worth grading from an inert one: this corpus has graded an unrostered /date as advisory precisely because /date is inert, while noting that an unrostered authority-bearing field would be a SHOULD-FIX. /sliceStanding is authority-bearing here. This artifact also invites the finding itself: reviewGuidance says 'Attack any silent v1-to-v2 path outside basedOn.method / honestyRepairsFromV1.'
shouldFix.mitigationIAcknowledge: The three changes are disclosed in prose at honestyRepairsFromV1[4] ('D-096 is an owner grant not a deferral; no sealed-row claim; keychain unexercised in first slice'), so nothing is concealed and I am not alleging a covert edit. Under the artifact's own two-source test the path is not silent. But basedOn.method's closure sentence is unconditional and self-contained — it does not read 'except paths named in honestyRepairsFromV1' — and it is that sentence which is refuted. The corpus precedent is that both the roster and the repair list must name every substantive path, and that a one-complete-change-roster defect is graded, not waived.

coordinatorNote: v2 repairs all three of my v1 findings properly, and I confirmed each by measurement rather than by reading the repair claim. The S-1 repair is the one that mattered and it took the harder-but-cleaner option: the unsourced obligation is removed outright — the single removal in the entire document — and replaced by a routing statement whose every clause checks out on live bytes, which leaves authorityClaim's three-item enumeration accurate without needing to widen it. The CFG-6/TM note lands the exact distinction that was missing, and file 02 is properly rostered. What blocks ACCEPT is new and narrow. basedOn.method declares a closed roster and closes with an unconditional sentence that every unnamed path is unchanged; a full recursive path diff refutes it, because /sliceStanding changed in three places and appears on neither the roster nor the succession-metadata carve-out. The same roster names /date and /authorityClaim, neither of which moved, so it is inaccurate in both directions at once. I want to be fair about two things: the three sliceStanding changes are genuine improvements and each is independently true, and they are disclosed in prose at honestyRepairsFromV1, so nothing is concealed. But the roster is what bounds a re-read, and the field it omits is the one carrying this artifact's D-096 (A) language — the single thing every dispatch in this corpus warns about. That is real cost, and it is the distinction this corpus already draws between an inert unrostered path and an authority-bearing one. The fix is one line in basedOn.method and changes the artifact's position not at all. One further note for the record: the review-prompt's stated HEAD is stale relative to the live 8daa2e6, and C-D110 has moved the COORD pin since v2 was authored; I re-checked both named properties against the live file and both survive, so nothing turns on it. 0 blockers, 1 SHOULD-FIX, 3 advisories: REJECT.
